chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Talha ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'The market of the Muslims is like their mosque, so whoever precedes to a place is more rightful to it until the night,' and he (peace be upon him) did not charge rent upon the rooms of the marketplace.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)
key_terms.سُوقُ الْمُسْلِمِينَ: The market of the Muslims (public marketplace)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling regarding occupancy rights and rent in public markets according to the Imams?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi outlines the customary law (urf) of the marketplace, equating its temporary occupancy rights to the sanctity and precedence found in mosques. It highlights Imam Ali’s (AS) practice of not charging rent for market stalls, thereby promoting economic accessibility and preventing monopolization by the wealthy. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on fair trade practices and the communal nature of public commercial spaces.
